Subject: Questions on termination / auto-renew language (Order Form A42)

Hi Soojin,

Quick follow on from procurement: our finance and legal teams are comfortable with most of the order form but have two stickier asks around auto-renew and termination-for-convenience.

1) Auto-renew trigger: they want explicit confirmation of the action that counts as "notice to not renew" (e.g., written notice to contracts@redwood.com vs. portal toggle). Can you confirm what of these we support operationally?

2) One-off waiver / exception: for pilot accounts we'd like the ability to get a one-off waiver of the auto-renew (e.g., during a negotiated extension) without an amendment cycle. What's your internal approval path and timing for granting a waiver? Will we need legal signoff + procurement PO?

Attached is the Order Form with their inline comments (redline). Can someone on your side propose a short operational playbook we can include in SOW appendices?

Thanks,
Maya
General Counsel, Ava Solutions

Soojin — ops notes below.

1) Notice channels: we currently process cancellations if we receive a written email to contracts@redwood.com or an action through the self-serve portal that toggles "do not renew." The portal action triggers a confirmation email (automated) that is recorded in our system.

2) Timing / SLO: portal toggles are processed immediately (system action), the confirmation email is generated within 15 minutes. Email notices to contracts@redwood.com are processed by contracts support within 1 business day and we send an acknowledgement that becomes the effective notice timestamp.

3) Proration / billing: if notice is received before the renewal effective date, we prorate final invoice based on unused committed seats for Dedicated plans; for hosted API monthly subscriptions we stop billing at the end of the current billing cycle unless a prorated refund is explicitly requested. For pilots we typically waive final month billing if waiver is approved in writing.

If legal prefers a single canonical method, we can recommend "written notice to contracts@redwood.com; portal actions are treated as written notice but require a confirmation email from Redwood to be effective." That preserves operations safety and gives Ava the portal convenience.

-Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability (Redwood Dedicated Ops)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Maya R. (Ava Solutions, GC) <maya.r@avasolutions.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on termination / auto-renew language (Order Form A42)

Maya — thanks for the clear notes and redline. We reviewed and propose two short options below you can pick from; both are intentionally brief so they can sit in the order form SOW appendix.

Option A (preferred by Legal & Ops):
"Either party may terminate this Order Form by providing written notice to the other party at contracts@redwood.com. Actions initiated via the customer portal are treated as "written notice" for convenience, provided Redwood issues a written confirmation to the customer within one (1) business day. The notice will be effective on the date Redwood sends the confirmation email. No additional amendment is required to effectuate termination under this section."

Option B (customer-favored — portal-first):
"This Order Form will automatically renew at the end of the then-current term unless the Customer either (a) disables automatic renewal in the Redwood customer portal prior to the renewal date, or (b) provides written notice to contracts@redwood.com. Portal actions are effective immediately; email notices are effective upon Redwood's written acknowledgment. Any waiver of automatic renewal for pilot or promotional accounts must be documented in writing and approved by Redwood's Finance and Legal teams."

Waiver workflow (appendix language suggestion):
"For one-off waivers of automatic renewal (e.g., pilot extensions), the Customer must request a waiver in writing to contracts@redwood.com and their Redwood account team. Redwood will escalate the waiver request to Finance and Legal. Standard approval authority: (i) Sales Ops or Revenue Operations for requests not impacting >15% of committed ARR; (ii) VP Sales or Finance sign-off for requests >15% or where billing refunds are requested. Redwood aims to provide a decision within five (5) business days of receipt. Approved waivers will be documented as a sealed addendum signed by authorized representatives of both parties or via a DocuSign link."

We attached a short playbook (auto_renew_waiver_playbook_v1.docx) that maps the internal approvers and the expected timeline. If Ava prefers one of these options, we can incorporate it into the redline and re-share.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
